thread.title: Wall Street in for a struggle to shake off last week’s losses as stock futures fall

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Wall Street in for a struggle to shake off last week’s losses as stock futures fall
text:
U.S. stocks fell sharply Monday, as investors looked past evidence of a still-strong U.S. economy to worry about growing evidence of a global economic slowdown and the effects of a U.S.-China trade dispute.
Benchmarks The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -1.58% fell 459 points or 1.9%, 23,3919, while the S&P 500 SPX, -1.24% is down 45 points, or 1.7% to 2,588. The Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -0.54% retreated 76 points, or 1.1%, to 6,892.
On Friday , the Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled 558.72 points, or 2.2%, to close at 24,388.95, the S&P 500 index retreated 2.3%, to 2,633.08, while the Nasdaq Composite Index slumped 3% to finish at 6,969.25.
That capped a week wherein all three major benchmarks saw their largest weekly percentage declines since March, and in which both the Dow and the S&P fell into negative territory for 2018.
Market drivers Concerns over global growth took center stage again Monday, after new data showing a sharp slowdown in Chinese export growth reinforced fears of Wall Street that the best of the current bull market is behind us.
That’s despite numerous data that support the bull case that the U.S. economy. at least, could continue to grow at a healthy pace into next year and beyond, including survey data from manufacturers and service providers showing resilient demand and a healthy U.S. consumer.
But trade worries have also been getting in the way of traditional end-of-year gains. China’s Vice Foreign Minister Le Yucheng summoned the U.S. ambassador on Sunday to insist the U.S. withdraw its arrest warrant on Huawei’s chief financial officer Meng Wanzhou, who was detained on Dec. 1 in Canada.
Read: Huawei arrest creates concerns in Silicon Valley as well as abroad
Some are worried that the Huawei executive’s arrest, news of which triggered sharp losses for Wall Street and global markets last week, will make it tough for China to follow through on trade concessions to the U.S. Investors are already dubious over how much progress was made between the two countries at the recent G-20 meeting.
Fears of an escalating trade conflict were also compounded by comments from U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer, who told CBS’ Face the Nation on Sunday that he considers the 90-day moratorium from new tariffs granted to the Chinese a “hard deadline,” and that the administration is not considering delaying an escalation of the trade conflict if the two sides can’t agree to an armistice by March 1st.
Opinion: The stock market is overreacting because fears about the economy are overblown
Investors are also increasingly focusing on the Dec. 18-19 Federal Reserve meeting, where the central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates. Comments from Fed Chairman Jerome Powell will be in the spotlight, and if he strikes a more conciliatory tone, hinting at a slowing of future hikes, it could spark the highly anticipated Santa rally, bullish investors say.
British Prime Minister Theresa May confirmed a decision to postpone a vote on her plan for the U.K. to exit from the European Union, potentially adding another complication to the fraught Brexit process. Investors will also watch negotiations between Italy and the EU over Rome’s planned budget deficit.
What are the analysts saying? “Today’s selloff is a continuation of Friday,” Doug Cohen, portfolio manager with Athena Capital Group told MarketWatch, when no amount of good news was able to distract investors from their growing fears over slowing global growth.
Oil prices have risen in December, Cohen said, but “not because of rising demand,” while the Fed’s dovish turn of late underscores “evidence that growth of the U.S. economy is slowing,” as much as it gives equity investors hope that interest rates won’t rise significantly from here, he said.
“The majority of the news last week [was] net positive,” Tom Essaye, president of the Sevens Report, wrote in a Monday note to clients.
“There won’t be 25% tariffs on Jan 1, and momentum toward a deal appears to be building, as the jobs report was solid but not too hot, while ISM Manufacturing PMIs were strong, and the Fed is shifting more and more dovish,” he wrote.
“Hopes of fruitful trade negotiations have taken a beating since the optimism that was around a week ago when the Buenos Aires G-20 meeting prompted hope of a rally into the end of the year for equities,” said Kit Juckes, global macro strategist at Société Générale, in a note. But he added that as Mondays are often an extension of what happened Friday, the rest of the week can't be judged too heavily on one session.
Stocks in focus Shares of Tesla Inc. TSLA, -0.21% are in focus after Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk appeared on “60 Minutes,” defending himself and the company from what he referred to as “relentless criticism.” Musk said he set and made a production target of 5,000 Model 3s a week and made the company itself profitable. Shares are down 0.6% Friday morning.
Apple Inc . AAPL, -2.21% stock is in focus after a key supplier, Japan Display Inc. JNNDF, -0.46% said it was cutting production for crystal display panels for the iPhone XR.
The company is also the focus of a dispute with Qualcomm Inc . QCOM, +3.59% after the chip maker announced that a Chinese court ordered Apple to stop selling older iPhone models in the country due to patent infringement. Apple stock is down 2% Friday, while Qualcomm stock is up 2.8%
Axovant Sciences Ltd . AXON, -25.14% stock is falling more than 27% early Monday, after the drugmaker announced that a trial of a treatment for REM sleep behavior disorder wasn’t successful.
Shares of German chemical producer BASF SE BAS, -1.29% are falling 4.4% Monday, after the firm warned that its profits would fall between 15% and 20% in 2018.
Aurora Cannabis Inc . ACB, -2.78% shares are in focus Monday after it said that it has entered a letter of intent to buy Mexico’s Farmacias Magistrales SA in a stock deal. The stock is down 1.8%.
Shares of Linde Plc . LIN, +1.73% are rising 1.6% Monday, after the multinational chemical company announced a $1 billion share repurchase program. Shares are up 2.5% in premarket trade.
What data are in focus? The Labor Department said U.S. job openings rose to 7.08 million in October , from 6.96 million a month earlier.
Other markets Asian markets were under fresh pressure on Monday, with China’s Shanghai Composite Index SHCOMP, -0.82% dropping 0.8% and the Nikkei 225 index NIK, -2.12% down 2.1%. European markets SXXP, -1.81% were under pressure.
U.S. crude oil CLF9, -2.09% CLF9, -2.09% prices were lower, while gold GCG9, -0.14% was flat, and the U.S. dollar DXY, +0.55% rose 0.3%.
